fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Open Green Space; Access Drive; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Multiple Structures; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow fire apparatus to reach the main residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Mark or designate a turnaround area near the detached structure so responding crews do not need to back out to the road.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and detached structure clear to allow responders to move on foot between structures quickly.
• Install a reflective address marker at the detached structure identifying it as a separate building on the property.
• Keep the access drive surface in condition that supports the weight of fire apparatus and ambulances year-round.
• Confirm the access drive width is sufficient to allow an apparatus to pass a parked vehicle without stopping.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Grass Cover; Scattered Trees; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Clear grass and low vegetation from directly around the base of the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin scattered shrubs near structures to increase open space between plants and buildings.
• Trim lower branches on trees closest to the house to reduce the path fire can travel from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Mow or cut grass across the property regularly, especially during dry periods, to keep it short and reduce the amount of burnable material near the house.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs so vehicles can move through without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate quickly from the road.
• Clear vegetation along the rear of the property to create a path that allows movement around the back of the house.
• Remove any dead grass, dry plant material, or debris that has collected near the foundation, under decks, or against exterior walls.
• Separate any wood piles, outdoor furniture, or stored materials from the exterior walls of the house.
